title: I Followed the Gym Day-Pass Fine Print After They Sold Me Three

parts.text: I bought a day pass at 6:45 a.m. because I was visiting. The desk sold me another at noon when I came back after a meeting, and a third at 5 because the first two "expired at close of session." I was thirty-one. Each pass was twenty-two dollars. The fine print on the back said a day pass is valid until facility close the same calendar day. I laid the three receipts on the desk. The closer, Josh, said sessions are whatever the manager says. The manager was Josh. Then he scanned my third pass and the computer flashed DUPLICATE DAY.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The computer already knew a day is a day; he had sold it three times.

social.video_title: They sold me the same day three times — Part 1/2
social.description: Visitor, three receipts, twenty-two dollars each, and a screen that said duplicate. Would you have left after the second?

parts.text: I asked for a refund of passes two and three. Josh offered store credit. I asked for the card. Corporate chat on the receipt agreed with the fine print. Forty-four dollars came back. I finished a deadlift under a fluorescent light that did not care about sessions. Josh learned to read the back of his own paper. I still travel with shoes. I buy one day when I mean one day. Close of session is not a calendar.

social.video_title: Corporate agreed with the back of the pass — Part 2/2
social.description: Two refunds, one workout, fluorescent peace. Was a session a date?
